sections.1:
This Solution Blueprint defines the Phase 1 scope for Archlin’s investment in integrated supply management capabilities for its specialty chemicals manufacturing business.

Archlin currently operates with an integrated planning environment with some automation, supported by SAP S/4HANA as the enterprise ERP system, but continues to experience poor inventory planning as a key business pain point.

The Phase 1 implementation is focused on Supply Management and is intended to strengthen Archlin’s ability to determine total requirements for products and raw materials, generate supply plans, and support procurement execution through purchase order and purchase requisition planning processes.

The solution direction for Archlin is to use Kinaxis Maestro capabilities to support supply planning and order management processes, including planning through bill of material structures where applicable, identifying supply requirements for purchased products and raw materials, and improving planning visibility across supply management activities.

Archlin’s supply management solution will be designed to work with SAP S/4HANA as the system of record for relevant enterprise data, with planning inputs, master data, transactional data, and planning outputs aligned to the implementation design confirmed during blueprinting.

The blueprint establishes the functional foundation for Archlin’s Phase 1 implementation by documenting the intended planning process, key assumptions, integration considerations, and expected business outcomes for supply management.

The implementation will prioritize standard Kinaxis Maestro capabilities where fit for Archlin’s supply management requirements, with any extensions or configuration decisions evaluated against Archlin’s business rules, SAP S/4HANA integration needs, and the objective of improving inventory planning performance.

Archlin’s expected outcomes from Phase 1 include improved visibility to supply requirements, better alignment between demand signals and supply actions, more structured planning of purchased materials, and a stronger foundation for inventory planning governance within the specialty chemicals manufacturing supply chain.

Details such as Archlin’s specific site list, product hierarchy, supplier segmentation, bill of material scope, planning calendars, and detailed integration objects are and will need to be confirmed during the implementation phase.
sections.1.1:
1.1 Company Background and Implementation Context

Archlin is a specialty chemicals manufacturing company operating with SAP S/4HANA as its enterprise resource planning platform.

Archlin’s current planning maturity is characterized by integrated planning with some automation, while inventory planning remains a key business pain point requiring improvement.

Archlin is investing in a Phase 1 supply management capability to strengthen planning discipline, improve supply visibility, and establish a more reliable foundation for inventory decisions within its SAP S/4HANA-enabled operating environment.

The current-state challenge for Archlin is poor inventory planning, which can limit the effectiveness of supply management decisions and reduce confidence in planned inventory positions across the planning horizon.

The Phase 1 solution scope for Archlin is focused on supply management, with emphasis on enabling more structured supply planning processes, improving alignment between supply decisions and inventory objectives, and supporting a more consistent planning operating model.

The implementation approach for Archlin will align the future-state supply management design to its existing SAP S/4HANA landscape and current integrated planning maturity, while identifying where automation and process standardization can improve inventory planning outcomes.

The expected business outcome for Archlin is improved supply management effectiveness through better inventory planning discipline, clearer planning visibility, and a scalable planning foundation for future supply chain capability enhancements.

sections.1.2:
Current State of Business

Archlin operates in the specialty chemicals manufacturing industry with SAP S/4HANA as its core ERP system and a planning environment that is currently partially automated, siloed, and heavily dependent on Excel-based processes.

Archlin’s current planning process requires planners to spend significant time consolidating forecasts and planning inputs from multiple regions, and Archlin does not currently have a centralized planning platform across North America and Europe.

Archlin’s current forecast accuracy is approximately 68%, and limited forecast visibility contributes to inventory levels that are higher than target.

Archlin’s manual and spreadsheet-based planning processes create delays in monthly planning cycles and limit timely collaboration between sales, operations, and supply chain teams.

Archlin’s key business pain point for this phase is poor inventory planning, including limited visibility to inventory targets, excess and obsolete exposure, slow-moving inventory, stock-out recovery, and root-cause analysis of inventory exceptions.

Archlin is investing in Kinaxis RapidResponse to establish a more integrated planning capability aligned with its SAP S/4HANA environment, with Phase 1 focused on Supply Management.

Archlin’s Phase 1 Supply Management scope is expected to improve planner visibility into demand and supply alignment, supply orders, material shortages, constraints, inventory positions, and exceptions that require action.

Archlin’s target solution direction includes the ability for planners to view period-ending inventory in value and volume, define and adjust inventory targets, identify slow-moving, excess, and obsolete inventory, analyze stock-out recovery, simulate corrective actions, and collaborate on inventory exceptions.

Archlin’s implementation will require master data and integration alignment with SAP S/4HANA so that supply planning, inventory planning, planning parameters, bills of material, part-source data, constraints, and supply orders can support effective decision-making in Kinaxis RapidResponse.

Archlin’s expected business outcomes from the Phase 1 Supply Management implementation include improved inventory planning discipline, better cross-functional visibility, faster exception identification, stronger support for supply decision-making, and a more scalable foundation for future planning maturity.
sections.1.3:
1.3 Scope

Archlin's Phase 1 scope for the RapidResponse implementation is focused on Supply Management for its specialty chemicals manufacturing business.

Archlin's current planning environment is partially automated and operates across siloed systems, with poor inventory planning identified as the primary business pain point to be addressed in this phase.

Archlin's blueprint scope defines the prescribed supply management processes, planning capabilities, and supporting resources required to establish the baseline for the future-state planning model.

Archlin's RapidResponse solution scope includes establishing a common planning terminology and operating model for Archlin business and IT stakeholders, aligned to foundational RapidResponse planning capabilities and prescribed data interfaces.

Archlin's source system for the scoped planning integration is SAP S/4HANA, and the detailed integration design, data mapping, and automation approach will be defined as part of the solution and technical blueprint activities.

Archlin's implementation scope includes documenting the user stories, analytics, and solution configuration details required to support the Supply Management release.

Archlin's solution blueprint will be updated during implementation to reflect approved requirement changes and solution design decisions for the scoped release.

Archlin's blueprint at technical go-live is intended to represent both the confirmed requirements and the implemented RapidResponse solution design for the Phase 1 Supply Management scope.

Archlin's expected outcome from this scope is an improved foundation for inventory planning, better visibility into supply management processes, and a more integrated planning environment than the current siloed planning landscape.

sections.1.4:
Archlin’s Phase 1 scope is focused on Supply Management for Archlin’s specialty chemicals manufacturing supply chain, with the blueprint addressing the inventory planning and supply visibility limitations currently experienced across Archlin’s partially automated, siloed planning environment and Excel-based processes.

Archlin’s current planning landscape includes SAP S/4HANA as the ERP system and source-aligned part master data containing Archlin materials, sites, buyer codes, planner codes, planning calendars, source rules, material types, units of measure, standard costs, safety stock quantities, product hierarchy attributes, and part classes. Archlin’s source extracts include finished goods and raw material records across multiple Archlin site codes, including examples such as V305, V318, V218, Q111, Q322, S302, S303, Z104, Z302, N235, N323, Q344, T321, V109, V110, V116, V127, and V307. Archlin’s extracted part data includes specialty chemical materials such as Liquid Caustic Soda, Sodium Hypochlorite, Calcium Chloride, Sulfuric Acid, Potassium Hydroxide, Sodium Hydrosulphide, Sodium Sulphide, Phosphoric Acid, Monoethanolamine, and other Archlin-managed chemical items represented in the uploaded part master extracts.

**Phase 1 Supply Management Scope**

| Scope Area | Archlin Phase 1 Scope Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Business focus | Archlin Phase 1 Supply Management for specialty chemicals manufacturing planning. |
| ERP alignment | Archlin SAP S/4HANA data alignment for supply planning master data and relevant planning attributes. |
| Planning maturity addressed | Archlin’s partially automated planning processes, siloed systems, and Excel-based planning workarounds. |
| Primary pain points addressed | Archlin’s poor inventory planning and limited supply visibility. |
| Data sources evidenced | Archlin uploaded part master extracts from Export Part.xlsx and RR export.xlsx. |
| Material scope evidenced | Archlin raw material and finished goods part records. |
| Site scope evidenced | Archlin site-level part planning records, including V305, V318, V218, Q111, Q322, S302, S303, Z104, Z302, N235, N323, Q344, T321, V109, V110, V116, V127, and V307. |
| Planning attributes evidenced | Archlin buyer code, planner code, planning calendar, source rule, type, unit of measure, standard cost, safety stock, days of supply, product hierarchy, and part class attributes. |

Archlin’s Phase 1 solution scope will establish a structured supply management planning foundation using the Archlin part and site planning attributes available in the uploaded extracts. Archlin’s supply planning model will use Archlin material-site combinations, Archlin planner segmentation, Archlin buyer ownership, Archlin planning calendars, Archlin source rules, Archlin material classifications, and Archlin inventory parameters to improve supply visibility and provide a more consistent basis for inventory planning decisions.

Archlin’s Phase 1 implementation scope follows the project delivery progression applicable to the Archlin blueprint, with scope definition, configuration alignment, confirmation, readiness, closeout, and support activities tied to the Archlin Supply Management deployment. Archlin’s scope confirmation will focus on validating the Archlin planning data and supply management design against the uploaded Archlin part master attributes and the stated Archlin business pain points of poor inventory planning and limited visibility.

Archlin’s implementation scope includes the configuration and validation activities required to make Archlin supply data usable for planning visibility, inventory review, and supply management decision support. Archlin’s implementation scope includes review of Archlin material-site data completeness, alignment of Archlin buyer and planner responsibility fields, validation of Archlin planning calendars and source rules, confirmation of Archlin material class usage, and reconciliation of Archlin inventory parameters that drive supply management outcomes.

Archlin’s Phase 1 scope excludes any demand planning, S&OP planning, manufacturing scheduling, distribution optimization, transportation planning, and advanced optimization capabilities unless those capabilities are explicitly added to the Archlin Phase 1 Supply Management scope through formal project change control. Archlin’s Phase 1 scope also excludes any assumptions about Archlin facilities, product lines, markets, or organisational entities that are not evidenced in the uploaded Archlin source documents.

| S&OP planning | Out of scope unless formally added for Archlin. |
| Manufacturing scheduling | Out of scope unless formally added for Archlin. |
| Distribution optimization | Out of scope unless formally added for Archlin. |
| Transportation planning | Out of scope unless formally added for Archlin. |

Archlin’s expected Phase 1 outcomes are improved supply management visibility, more structured inventory planning inputs, clearer planner and buyer accountability, and a more consistent planning data foundation for Archlin’s specialty chemicals supply chain. Archlin’s Phase 1 outcomes will be measured against the ability to reduce reliance on disconnected Excel-based planning views, improve visibility across Archlin material-site combinations, and create a validated foundation for subsequent planning capability expansion if Archlin elects to extend the program beyond Phase 1 Supply Management.
